---
title: "Architecture"
subtitle: "ESPN cross-league core, the parser layer, and the codegen pipeline"
---

`sportsdataverse-py` is built around a small set of reusable cores rather than
hundreds of hand-written scrapers. This page summarizes that architecture and
the codegen pipeline that drives the production documentation — the part most
relevant to a docs-toolchain evaluation.

## ESPN cross-league architecture

The cross-league ESPN wrapper surface lives in
`sportsdataverse/_common_espn.py`. The pattern is **one core + N thin
extensions**:

- `_common_espn.py` — ~80 core functions parameterized on `(sport, league)`
  slugs. Every ESPN URL family is wrapped once (Site v2 / Site v2 alt / Web v3 /
  Core v2 / Core v3 / CDN).
- `_UNIVERSAL_WRAPPERS` / `_NCAA_WRAPPERS` / `_FOOTBALL_WRAPPERS` /
  `_MLB_WRAPPERS` — tables of `(short_name, core_fn)` tuples mapped onto each
  league.
- `make_league_module(sport, league, prefix, namespace, …)` — iterates the
  wrapper tables and **registers each one dynamically** in the league module's
  namespace as `espn_{prefix}_{short}`.

Per-league extension modules (`sportsdataverse/{league}/{league}_espn_ext.py`)
are four-line files:

```python
# sportsdataverse/nba/nba_espn_ext.py
__all__ = make_league_module("basketball", "nba", "nba", globals())

# sportsdataverse/cfb/cfb_espn_ext.py — both NCAA + football extras
__all__ = make_league_module(
    "football", "college-football", "cfb", globals(),
    include_ncaa=True, include_football=True,
)
```

Total cross-league surface: **121 short names** registered across many leagues
= **800+ wrappers**.

::: {.callout-important}
This dynamic, namespaced generation is exactly what makes auto-introspection
documentation tools struggle with this package — there is no static `__all__` of
flat names to discover. See the [evaluation write-up](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py/blob/proto/quarto-docs/docs-quarto/README.md)
for how that shaped the Great-Docs result.
:::

## The parser layer

Every wrapper returns raw `Dict` by default (or, for parser-backed ESPN
endpoints, a tidy frame by default). The parser layer turns payloads into tidy
polars / pandas DataFrames. There are **six parser modules**, one per data
surface:

| Module | Surface |
|---|---|
| `_common_espn_parsers.py` | ESPN cross-league (Site v2 + Core v2 + Web v3) — 30+ dedicated + a 21-section summary dispatcher |
| `nhl/nhl_api_web_parsers.py` | `api-web.nhle.com/v1/` modern game-feed |
| `nhl/nhl_edge_parsers.py` | `api-web.nhle.com/v1/edge/*` player tracking |
| `nhl/nhl_stats_rest_parsers.py` + `nhl_records_parsers.py` | `api.nhle.com/stats/rest` + `records.nhl.com` |
| `mlb/mlb_api_parsers.py` | `statsapi.mlb.com` Stats API |
| `nfl/nfl_api_parsers.py` | `api.nfl.com` "Shield" data API |

**The parser contract is universal across all six modules:**

- Return `polars.DataFrame` by default; pandas via `return_as_pandas=True`.
- Empty / malformed payloads return a **zero-row frame** instead of raising — so
  callers can chain without null-checks.
- Output columns are snake-cased.

## The codegen pipeline (and what the docs are generated from)

Reference docs in the production site are **generated from the same YAML endpoint
metadata that drives the wrappers**, via the codegen CLI:

```bash
python tools/codegen/generate.py --docs    # rewrite the per-league reference subtree
python tools/codegen/generate.py --check   # CI drift gate: fail on stale generated docs
```

- **Endpoint YAML** lives in `tools/codegen/endpoints/*.yaml`
  (`espn_site_v2.yaml`, `espn_core_v2.yaml`, `mlb_api.yaml`, …). Each endpoint
  declares its path, params, `parser:`, and `returns_schema:`.
- **`@return` tables** come from `tools/codegen/schemas/*.yaml`
  (`col_name | type | description`).
- **Templates** (`tools/codegen/templates/_reference_block.jinja` + friends)
  render an 8-section per-function block into markdown for Docusaurus.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import yaml, pathlib

root = pathlib.Path().resolve()
# walk up to the repo root (where tools/codegen lives)
for _ in range(5):
    if (root / "tools" / "codegen" / "endpoints").exists():
        break
    root = root.parent

ep_dir = root / "tools" / "codegen" / "endpoints"
stems = ["espn_site_v2", "espn_web_v3", "espn_core_v2", "mlb_api"]
rows = []
for stem in stems:
    p = ep_dir / f"{stem}.yaml"
    if p.exists():
        d = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
        eps = d.get("endpoints", [])
        with_schema = sum(1 for e in eps if e.get("returns_schema"))
        rows.append((stem, len(eps), with_schema))

import polars as pl
pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=["endpoint_yaml", "n_endpoints", "with_returns_schema"], orient="row")
```

The table above is computed at build time by reading the **actual** endpoint
YAML in this repo — so it can't drift from the metadata it describes.

## How this maps onto a docs toolchain

This is the crux of the Quarto evaluation:

- **Generated reference** (Docusaurus today) → schema-table reference built from
  `returns_schema` YAML. Accurate column lists, but not *actual* `df.head()`
  output.
- **Executable reference** (Quarto here) → the example output a reader sees is
  the literal frame the code produced at build time. See the hand-written
  [MLB](reference/mlb.qmd) and [NBA](reference/nba.qmd) reference pages, and the
  generator-emitted [MLB stubs](reference/generated/index.qmd).

## Ecosystem

`sportsdataverse-py` is one package in a multi-language family:

- **Python:** `sportsdataverse-py` (this package).
- **R sisters:** [`hoopR`](https://hoopR.sportsdataverse.org),
  [`wehoop`](https://wehoop.sportsdataverse.org),
  [`cfbfastR`](https://cfbfastR.sportsdataverse.org),
  [`baseballr`](https://baseballr.sportsdataverse.org),
  [`fastRhockey`](https://fastRhockey.sportsdataverse.org).
- **JS:** `sportsdataverse-js`.

Because Quarto is the native literate-docs tool for the R world and also executes
Python, a single Quarto toolchain could in principle document the **R and Python**
packages with the same run-it-for-real model — a point explored in the
[evaluation](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py/blob/proto/quarto-docs/docs-quarto/README.md).
